security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel code (unwinder, signal delivery, kdb) computes frame-record offsets using XLEN_BYTES instead of sizeof(uintptr_t) when FreeBSD gains ILP32 or mixed-XLEN ABI support — on RV64ILP32, XLEN=64 but PTRSZ=32, causing the kernel to read return addresses and saved frame pointers at wrong offsets (fp-16/-8 instead of fp-8/-4), dereferencing garbage as control-flow targets.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: XLEN_BYTES|XLEN\b.*\bframe|\bfp\b.*\bXLEN in riscv/ tree combined with stack frame access
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD's unwind.c already uses sizeof(uintptr_t) (=PTRSZ) for frame-record offsets, making it spec-compliant, but riscvreg.h's XLEN_BYTES macro (XLEN/8) is a latent hazard: any future kernel code or ILP32 ABI support that uses XLEN_BYTES instead of sizeof(void*) for user-stack frame records would produce wrong offsets, enabling controlled stack-walk hijack and potential privilege escalation via crafted ILP32 binaries.

findings.finding: Uses sizeof(uintptr_t) via sizeof(fp) and uintptr_t* array indexing for frame-record offsets. No XLEN_BYTES in frame computation. Forward-compatible with ILP32.

User-space frame-record offsets hardcoded as sizeof(uint64_t) instead of sizeof(uintptr_t). On RV64ILP32, sizeof(uint64_t)=8 but sizeof(uintptr_t)=4, causing reads at fp-8/-16 instead of fp-4/-8, dereferencing garbage as control-flow targets. Currently benign on LP64-only FreeBSD.
findings.snippet:
pc = dtrace_fuword64((void *)(fp - 1 * sizeof(uint64_t)));
fp = dtrace_fuword64((void *)(fp - 2 * sizeof(uint64_t)));

findings.finding: Delegates frame-record walking entirely to unwind_frame(). Trapframe access uses struct fields (tf->tf_s[0], tf->tf_sepc), not XLEN-based offset computation.
Delegates all frame-record walking to unwind_frame(). No manual offset computation. Forward-compatible.

Uses XLEN_BYTES for ld/sd instruction width in data-copy loops. This is correct usage — XLEN controls register/memory-access width (ld needs 8-byte alignment on RV64). Not frame-related; not in scope.
findings.snippet:
li t2, XLEN_BYTES
blt a2, t2, 4f  /* Byte-copy if len < XLEN_BYTES */
...
ld a4, 0(a0)   /* Load word from src */
sd a4, 0(a1)   /* Store word in dest */

findings.finding: Signal delivery uses stack-aligned pointer arithmetic on struct sigframe*, not XLEN-based frame-record offset computation. No frame-record walking.
Definition: XLEN_BYTES = XLEN/8 = __riscv_xlen/8. Correct definition. Only risky if used for frame-record offset arithmetic (which it is not in the kernel unwinder; only in DTrace as noted above).
